body: Work as epxected: in JS `'' + null == 'null'`

In Angular 1.x I could just bind to a variable like this {{name}} and if name was null nothing was shown on screen.  

In Angular 2, {{name}} seems to output the word 'null' which may be as expected but isn't very friendly.  

I don't want to have to do something like {{name || ''}} in my templates.

Am I missing something here or is there another way to approach this?

Thanks, Simon

@vicb it is true that this is consistent with JS behaviour but I don't think this is what users would expect (at least I find it surprising) and it is not how things work in ng1.

I'm going to re-open this one so we can discuss. //cc: @mhevery

> @vicb it is true that this is consistent with JS behaviour but I don't think this is what users would expect (at least I find it surprising) and it is not how things work in ng1.

What would you expect, jus `''` in place of `'null'`?
Yep, empty string. This is how it is handled in ng1, no?
i dunno, I think there's value in matching the language itself (eg ``${null}`` -> `"null"`), but whatever people want to do

In templates it should definitely handle nulls and undefined with empty string... otherwise this needs to be done by the user on every place holder in every template.

pkozlowski-opensource is right, this is the behaviour in Angular 1.

What about it ? :D
Just compare it with `{{ value }}`.

## 

This is a really nice feature of ng1 (and one lots of developers are used to) and plays well with the elvis operator (which also everyone is used to from ng1 - well not the operator, just the behaviour (grrrr for introducing that btw)).

 TBH I haven't fiddled around much with ng2, so I don't know if the usefulness of defaulting to `''` has diminished.
`null` should be `""` (empty string) User should never see `null`
